blocks.source: Vol IV, Sensor Perception, § Capture Physics and Calibration
blocks.md: When photons from a warehouse rack upright strike the navigation camera's silicon detector, they do not become an instantaneous feature tensor in host memory. Before a neural backbone or state observer ever reads the frame, the photodiode array must accumulate charge over a finite exposure window, serialize rows off the sensor die, and move bytes across the interconnect, while the robot keeps moving through every millisecond of that process. In CMOS active-pixel sensors, incident photons generate electron-hole pairs through the photoelectric effect according to a wavelength-dependent quantum efficiency PhotodiodeQuantumEfficiency(OpticalWavelength).

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Observation age matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.

questions.q: The section **Capture Physics and Calibration** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.
Per-row pose interpolation for rolling shutters and per-point de-skew for LiDAR sweeps remove the motion a finite capture interval smears into geometry.

Each oscillator stamps time in its own clock domain, so a capture time can be checked only after conversion to the consumer's clock, and that conversion carries a measured bound (offset tail, path asymmetry, drift between syncs) that every age check adds.

Each observation is wrapped with capture time, clock id, clock-conversion bound, frame, payload, covariance, clearance inset, health bits, and CRC so a consumer can refuse it before reading a payload byte.
